api.dispatch: dispatch(call_id, job_id, role, phase) -> True for new durable dispatch; False for an identical already successful call; raises before execution when paused, pending, unplanned, skipped or conflicting.
api.complete: complete(call_id, record) -> preserved result dict; records success/failure, direct usage and pause state. An identical repeated completion is idempotent; a changed terminal record is rejected.
api.run: run(call_id, job_id, role, phase, invoke_callback) -> successful saved result dict; callback takes no arguments. A stopped/invalid result is saved then raises CallControlPaused with call_id, failure_kind and record attributes.
api.skip: skip(call_id, reason) -> True for a newly skipped undispatched planned call; False for the identical prior skip. Different reason, dispatched or unplanned calls reject.
api.report: report() -> fixed public call/usage/coverage report. Decisions are pause_calls, wait, report_results. No logical-job quality inference.
api.snapshot: snapshot() -> defensive copy of checkpoint state.
api.record: record(call_id) -> defensive copy of saved original result or None.

integration_contract: Keep existing runner stop guards, raw event capture and source/hash verification. The adapter adds a durable call boundary; it does not replace those checks.
Map each physical CLI call to one reducer session. Keep logical job, role and phase as separate metadata; adaptive selection/follow-up calls and batched judges are separate invocations.
Use a dedicated controller output directory and the same ordered planned_call_ids on restore. Optional retrieval calls can be explicitly skipped with a reason.

Persist dispatch before invoking the callback. A restored unresolved call blocks every new dispatch until explicitly reconciled outside this API; never infer that a crash means no provider call happened.

Return saved stopped result dictionaries from callback, or attach them to exception.record, so known failed-attempt direct usage is preserved. A generic exception without a saved result remains unknown and pauses.
Success requires status complete and one valid direct_terminal_usage record; absent direct fields are never filled from normalized/fallback usage.
Skip records are separate from the reducer request/event ledger and add no usage. Plan completion requires successful calls plus explicit skips to cover the plan; any pause takes precedence.
Restore is idempotent for already successful calls; metadata, plan and terminal-record conflicts fail closed. Existing caller verification of raw saved files should still occur before reuse.
persistence: JSON checkpoint replacement is atomic and fsynced before the callback. A POSIX file lock serializes ledger updates, and only one unresolved call may exist. Progress is derived and rebuilt from the authoritative checksum-verified checkpoint on restore.
limitations: Serial local POSIX checkpoint adapter; no distributed worker or concurrent provider scheduling claim.
The frozen reducer quality/provider-retry fields are not exposed as benchmark quality. Job/role/phase metadata retains physical-call distinctions.
Skipped optional calls resolve plan coverage without producing request or usage events.
A restored in-flight call fails closed and needs explicit reconciliation; there is no automatic retry/resume.
An exception without an attached saved result has unknown usage. Callers should return a stopped saved result or attach exception.record to preserve known failed-attempt usage.
This offline validation does not measure notification delivery or real-time provider-error detection latency. Existing runner safeguards remain in place.
